floor_history.headline: recon: baseline floor=2 reconfirmed at HEAD 08f1aa37; 2-insn diff = mflo dest ($8 vs target $5) + dependent sra src at offsets 0xC4/0xCC; frontier built with 3 mechanism-grounded un-tried hypotheses

frontier.hypothesis: Instrumented allocno-priority dump will explain why the t-mult pseudo (~104 per prior notes) is placed in $8 instead of the dying a1(=4096); the question is a specific liveness/tiebreaker one, not a general wall
frontier.mechanism: Build tmp/gccdbg/cc1 with BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG / BB2_PRIO_DEBUG per memory/project/register-alloc-deep-dive.md. Compile an isolated standalone of rob_life_ctrl_2 (single-function preprocess of text1a_c.c) with the debug cc1. Read (a) allocno-priority table entry for the t-mult pseudo, (b) its conflict list at that point, (c) the 0x1000-constant pseudo's live range around 0xB0-0xC4. If the dump shows a global.c:624 priority-tiebreaker wall (cpu_side_move_dir_4 / marionation_Exec class per register-alloc-deep-dive.md), that changes disposition; otherwise it names the exact lever to attack.
frontier.next_probe: 1) preprocess isolated .i for text1a_c.c; 2) build/patch tmp/gccdbg/cc1 with the debug macros; 3) run cc1 -da <flags> on the .i and dump the allocno/priority tables; 4) diff against a matched sibling in same file to isolate what's different

frontier.hypothesis: Extending the 0x1000 constant's live range so it dies EXACTLY at t's subu (0xB0) — without splitting the constant into a second pseudo (q's use at 0x88 must stay CSE'd with t's use) — will cause GCC RA to reuse a1 for the t-mult's mflo destination
frontier.mechanism: In target, `li a1,4096` is emitted once and used as minuend at three subu sites (0x88, 0xA0, 0xB0). The mflo at 0xC4 reuses a1 because pseudo(0x1000) dies at 0xB0 and pseudo(t-mult) is born at 0xC4 with a1 free. Any C form that (a) delays the 0x1000-constant pseudo's DEATH past t's subu, or (b) creates a second 0x1000 pseudo that q uses but t doesn't, would fail. So the C must keep exactly one 0x1000 pseudo, kill it at t's subu, and NOT introduce any competing live range in $8/t0 at 0xC4.
frontier.next_probe: After the ALLOCDBG dump names the priority tiebreaker at 0xC4, try C forms that (1) hoist the `0x1000 - ...` outer subtraction into a named s32 declared inline (`s32 tsub = 0x1000 - ((s * (0x1000 - f)) >> 12); t = (v * tsub) >> 12;`) and see whether the named intermediate's pseudo death changes the tiebreaker without duplicating the constant; (2) reorder the subexpression evaluation so the innermost `(0x1000 - f)` computes AFTER q's subu but before t's mult, keeping the outer constant use last

frontier.hypothesis: Retyping/narrowing the intermediate `(s * (0x1000 - f)) >> 12` — e.g. to a named `s16`/`u16` local — will change the t-mult pseudo's conflict graph enough to flip the tiebreaker, per Lever A/B of register-alloc-pure-c
frontier.mechanism: Pseudo 104's placement depends on its conflict set at 0xC4; adding a fresh short-lived narrower pseudo can perturb the priority function without changing emitted arithmetic (mult/sra still emit 32-bit ops for s16 promotion). If it produces the same bytes, it's a legitimate structural lever; if it changes bytes, it's ruled out.
frontier.next_probe: After the ALLOCDBG dump, test `s16 sf = (s16)(s * (0x1000 - f)); q = (v * (0x1000 - (sf >> 12))) >> 12;` and the analogous form for the t-subexpression; sandbox each; if bytes drift on the other 94 insns it's out; if only 0xC4/0xCC change, examine whether they moved TOWARD target.
